evidence: Posted "QA Automation Engineer" (Technology, Full-time, Remote, $150k-$100k, Selenium skill); appeared immediately in Employer Dashboard listings and in job-seeker homepage list (count went from 8 to 9 jobs).

actual: Submitted job with Minimum Salary=150000 and Maximum Salary=100000 (min > max). Form accepted it with no error message; job was published and displayed as "$150k - $100k" in both dashboard and job listing.

issue: Incorrect relative posting date for newly created job
actual: Job posted at 2026-08-24 16:12 UTC (current date 2026-08-24) displays posting date as "Yesterday" instead of "Today" in both employer dashboard and job listing.

evidence: Clicking the applications-count button (2) for "QA Automation Engineer" expanded an "Applications (2)" panel listing both submitted applications with applicant details.
Each application record shows name (e.g. "Test Applicant"), email, phone when provided (555-0199), message, and submission date ("Yesterday"), each as a distinct entry.
Submitting application for Test Applicant showed toast "Application submitted!" and the application appeared under QA Automation Engineer in employer dashboard with matching name/email/phone/message.

issue: Duplicate application with same email not blocked
actual: Submitted a second application to the same job (QA Automation Engineer) using the same email (test.applicant@example.com) as an existing application. It was accepted with the same "Application submitted!" success message and now appears as a second, separate application entry ("Duplicate Applicant") in the employer dashboard instead of being rejected.

evidence: Empty form submission blocked with "Please fill out this field." on Name/Email; invalid email "not-an-email" blocked with "Please include an '@' in the email address" native validation, field is highlighted/focused.

Submitted valid application (name, email, phone, message) and received clear toast confirmation "Application submitted! Your application for QA Automation Engineer at TechCorp Solutions has been sent."
Job details page for QA Automation Engineer displays title, company, industry, employment type, location, salary range, posting date, full description, and required skills.
Job cards on homepage (e.g. Senior Frontend Developer, QA Automation Engineer) show title, company, industry badge, employment type badge, location, salary range, posting date, and skill tags.
Dashboard shows 6 Active Jobs matching the 6 listed jobs, and Total Applications=5 matching sum of per-job counts (2+2+1+0+0+0=5).

issue: No edit functionality for published jobs
actual: Employer dashboard job cards only expose two controls: an applications-count toggle and a delete (trash) button. There is no edit/pencil icon or link, and clicking the job title does not navigate to an edit form. No way found to modify a published job's details.

evidence: Clicking delete showed confirmation dialog "Delete this job? This will permanently delete... and all its applications." Cancel preserved the job; confirming Delete removed "DevOps Engineer (Contract)" from employer dashboard (Active Jobs 6→5) and from job-seeker listing.
Homepage shows "Showing 8 jobs" matching actual 8 listed job cards; opening a listing (job details page tested earlier) navigates correctly with full details.
Industry=Technology → 2 jobs; +Location=San Francisco → 1 job; +Type=Remote → 0 jobs (no-results state); Clear filters restored to 8 jobs.
Each filter change immediately updated result count and list (8→2→1→0 with "No jobs found" message); Clear filters restored full list of 8 immediately.

Search "selenium" matched skill "Selenium" (1 result); "techcorp" matched company "TechCorp Solutions" (3 results); "NURSE" matched title "Registered Nurse" (1 result) - all case-insensitive and updated immediately.

issue: State does not persist across page reload
actual: After reloading http://localhost:6003/, all changes were lost: the newly published "QA Automation Engineer" job disappeared, and the previously deleted "DevOps Engineer (Contract)" job reappeared. The listing reverted to the original 8 seed jobs, indicating jobs, applications, and deletions are stored only in memory and not persisted.
